segments.caption: A news report graphic for "NEW DETAILS" introduces a multi-vehicle accident on a highway in Douglasville, Georgia, where a red car is severely damaged after a collision with a large truck. Emergency responders and a tow truck are on scene, managing the aftermath as traffic continues to flow on the adjacent lanes.

An aerial view captures the aftermath of a serious collision in Douglasville, Georgia, where a red car is crushed and wedged beneath the front of a stopped freight train on the tracks. Emergency personnel, including police and tow truck operators, are on the scene, with police cars blocking traffic on the adjacent highway. The incident, involving a train and a vehicle, appears to be the focus of a news report, as indicated by the on-screen graphics.

An aerial news report captures the aftermath of a train collision with a red car on a railroad track in Douglasville, Georgia. The scene shows the damaged vehicle crushed under the front of a locomotive, with emergency responders and police cars on the adjacent road. The report then transitions to a map graphic pinpointing the incident's location near Atlanta.

A news report details a train collision with a car in Douglasville, Georgia, at the intersection of E Broad St and Mozley St. The segment begins with a map graphic pinpointing the incident location near highways 78 and 20, then transitions to a live reporter on scene, providing on-the-ground updates.

A CBS Atlanta news reporter stands outdoors at night, delivering a live report on a train collision with a car. The scene is framed by a graphic map highlighting the incident location at the intersection of E Broad St and Mozley St in Douglasville, near the crossings of I-78 and I-20. The on-screen headline “TRAIN HITS CAR” and the station’s logo confirm the breaking news nature of the segment.

A CBS Atlanta news reporter, Steve Kiggins, delivers a live on-site report at night from the scene of a train collision with a car in Douglasville, Georgia. The broadcast graphic identifies the location as the intersection of E Broad St and Mozley St, while the reporter stands on the roadside holding a microphone, providing new details about the incident.

A CBS Atlanta news reporter, Steve Kiggins, delivers live on-air updates from Douglasville, Douglas County, at night. Standing outdoors on a dark street, he speaks into a microphone as the lower third graphic transitions from his name to the location, indicating he is reporting on a developing story.

A CBS Atlanta news reporter delivers a live on-scene report from a dark, empty street in Douglasville, Douglas County, at night. He gestures toward the road as he speaks, providing new details about a developing story.

A live news report from Douglasville, Douglas County, at night, shows a quiet, curved road illuminated by streetlights, with a reporter gesturing toward the scene as the camera pans slowly along the road.

A live news report from Douglasville, Georgia, at night, shows a road intersection with a train derailment. The footage transitions from a live shot of the scene to an aerial view revealing a train car and a red vehicle involved in a collision on the tracks, with emergency personnel and a police car present.

An aerial view captures the aftermath of a collision between a red car and the front of a black CSX train at a railroad crossing. Emergency personnel in safety vests are on the scene, and a blue police vehicle is parked nearby on the adjacent road. The sequence then cuts to a close-up interview with a woman, presumably a witness or victim, who is smiling as she speaks to a reporter.

A news report captures the aftermath of a train derailment at a busy intersection in Atlanta. A woman and a man are interviewed on the scene, with the man gesturing toward the incident. The main event is shown with workers in high-visibility vests inspecting the derailed freight train car, which is lying on the tracks amidst traffic and railway signals.

A news report from Atlanta documents a train derailment at a railroad crossing. In the first frame, a railroad worker in a safety vest inspects a derailed freight car on the tracks, while another worker is visible nearby. The subsequent frames focus on a local resident, Robert Woods, who is interviewed on-site near the crossing. He gestures toward the area, likely describing the incident, as traffic continues to pass by the damaged tracks. The overall scene depicts an active emergency response

A man named Robert Woods, identified by a news chyron as living near the crossing, stands on the side of a road and gestures with his right arm toward a railroad crossing with active traffic signals and moving vehicles. The scene is set in Atlanta, as indicated by the station logo, on an overcast day with a temperature of 48 degrees.

A man points urgently toward the scene of a train collision with a red car on the tracks in Douglasville, Georgia, as aerial footage shows the aftermath of the crash involving a train and a car on the tracks.

A red sedan is shown severely damaged after a collision with a train in Douglasville, Douglas County. The car is lodged on the tracks, with its front end crushed, while the front of the train is also visibly impacted. The scene is captured from an aerial perspective, with news graphics from CBS Atlanta identifying the location and temperature.

An aerial view captures a dramatic collision where a red sedan is struck and pinned by the front of a large semi-truck on a railroad crossing. The car is severely damaged, with its hood crumpled and front end crushed, while the truck’s cab is positioned directly over the vehicle. A person is visible standing on the truck’s platform near the cab, observing the scene. The event appears to be a recent, high-impact accident, with the train tracks running diagonally

A red car is struck by a train on a railroad crossing in Atlanta, as shown in the first frame. The subsequent frames show a different, beige minivan driving through the same crossing, highlighting the dangerous and frequent nature of such intersections.

A news report from Atlanta shows a train track crossing a road, with cars passing by. A man in a black hoodie and cap stands at the intersection, speaking to the camera as traffic moves in the background, with the temperature displayed as 48 degrees.

A news reporter stands at a street intersection in Atlanta, delivering a live on-location report. He is dressed in a black hoodie and cap, speaking directly to the camera as vehicles pass by in the background. The overcast sky and the visible railroad tracks suggest a cool, possibly damp day, with the temperature displayed as 48°F. The scene is a typical urban street corner, with traffic lights and commercial buildings in the distance, providing context for the news story being covered.

A CBS Atlanta news report captures a scene at a railroad crossing in Atlanta, where a man in a hoodie speaks to the camera. The footage then cuts to utility workers in safety vests inspecting equipment near the tracks, followed by shots of traffic navigating the crossing. The segment documents a routine inspection and traffic flow at this urban rail intersection.

The frames depict a train derailment at a railroad crossing in Atlanta, transitioning from a daytime view of traffic crossing the tracks to a nighttime scene of the aftermath, where emergency responders are seen attending to damaged vehicles and debris on the tracks.

A news report from Atlanta shows a daytime scene at a road-rail intersection, where a white pickup truck is seen turning across the tracks, followed by other vehicles. The footage then cuts to a close-up of the railroad tracks, highlighting the area where the road crosses them.
A yellow school bus is shown driving across a railroad crossing, with close-up shots highlighting the damaged track and gravel bed where the rails have been displaced or broken.

A news report from Atlanta shows a damaged railroad crossing where a concrete curb has cracked and broken away, exposing the track and gravel below. A reporter stands nearby at the intersection, gesturing as he speaks, with traffic and streetlights visible in the background, highlighting a safety hazard at this urban railroad crossing.

A news reporter stands at a railroad crossing in Atlanta, gesturing toward the scene of a train collision with a red car. An aerial view shows the wreckage of the red sedan pinned between the train and the tracks, with emergency personnel and onlookers present.

An aerial view captures a dramatic train collision with a red car at a railroad crossing, with emergency personnel on scene. The segment then cuts to an on-the-ground interview with a man in a black hoodie, who appears to be a witness or involved party, speaking to the camera at the same intersection, where traffic signals and a white pickup truck are visible in the background.

A news reporter stands on a roadside near railroad tracks, reporting on a traffic accident. The scene shows two women watching from the side of the road, and a close-up of a red traffic light. The main event is a collision between a red car and a train, with the car lying on the tracks and a tow truck positioned nearby to remove it. The footage appears to be from a news report, indicated by the "Atlanta" and "cbsatlanta.com" watermark

An aerial view captures the aftermath of a collision at a railroad crossing, where a red car is pinned between a stopped train and a flatbed tow truck. Emergency personnel and bystanders are present as workers attempt to free the vehicle. The scene then cuts to a woman being interviewed on the roadside, providing a witness account of the incident.

A CBS Atlanta news reporter conducts an on-location interview at a street intersection during the day, followed by a separate nighttime report from the same location, where the reporter stands alone under artificial lights, delivering a report.

A CBS Atlanta news reporter, Steve Kiggins, delivers a live on-site report at night. Standing on a roadside, he speaks into a microphone while the lower third graphic identifies him, the station, and the location as Atlanta. The scene is dark, illuminated by artificial lighting, with traffic signals and distant buildings visible in the background.

A CBS Atlanta news reporter, Steve Kiggins, delivers a live on-air report from an outdoor location at night. He stands on a road, holding a microphone with the station's logo, speaking to the camera as the lower third graphic displays his name, email, and the "LIVE" and "NEW DETAILS" indicators.
